mlb.sp_quality.label: Starting-pitcher true-talent quality (SIERA/xFIP/Stuff+, projections)
mlb.sp_quality.mechanism: A starter's underlying ability to prevent runs per batter (K, BB, contact quality) determines run prevention for the innings he works.
mlb.sp_quality.rationale: Starter quality is the dominant single input for moneyline, total and F5 markets, but ERA is mostly noise over small samples; projections and skill-based estimators carry more signal. mlb.sp_workload.label: Expected innings / batters faced / pitch count
mlb.sp_workload.mechanism: Batters faced is the volume multiplier for every pitcher counting stat (strikeouts, outs, hits, walks, earned runs) and sets how much bullpen exposure the game has.
mlb.sp_workload.rationale: Pitcher props are rate x opportunity; workload uncertainty is often a bigger source of variance than rate uncertainty. Subtle: realized pitch count and pull are not knowable pregame; only their distribution is. mlb.pitch_mix.mechanism: What a pitcher throws and how well each pitch misses bats or induces weak contact is the mechanical source of strikeouts, hits and walks.

mlb.run_dist.label: Run-scoring distribution (inning-level, negative binomial) and correlations
mlb.run_dist.mechanism: Runs per team per game are overdispersed and inning-clustered, so threshold and total markets depend on distribution shape and the correlation between teams.

m.quote_history.label: Kalshi bid/ask/last time series (pre-game through close)
m.quote_history.mechanism: The traded price aggregates every participant's information about this contract, including injury and lineup news that moves faster than public stats.
m.quote_history.rationale: A price series is both a feature (the late price is usually a strong prior that model inputs must add to, not replace) and the reference for any edge claim. Subtle: the same last-trade price can be stale on thin MLB prop rungs, so bid/ask midpoints with timestamps matter more than last, and price movement after lineup/goalie/pitcher confirmation is information about what the news was worth.
m.quote_history.measurement: Store per-ticker candlesticks (bid, ask, last, volume) at 1-minute or finer resolution, align to scheduled start and to timestamps of lineup/starter confirmation; derive mid, spread, move since open, move since confirmation. Never use post-close values as pregame features.

m.orderbook_depth.label: Order-book depth and spread
m.orderbook_depth.mechanism: Depth and spread determine whether a modelled edge can be executed and how much the quoted price reflects informed versus noise flow.
m.orderbook_depth.rationale: Wide spreads and thin depth on MLB prop and long-tail rungs mean the midpoint is a noisy probability estimate and the edge after crossing the spread may be negative. Subtle: historical depth is only available if captured live, so the pregame view is whatever was snapshotted; reconstructing it from trades is approximate.
m.orderbook_depth.measurement: Snapshot the book (top-N levels both sides) at fixed intervals before start; compute spread, depth within 2 cents of mid, imbalance. Compare model edge to half-spread plus fee to get executable edge.

m.volume_oi.label: Volume and open interest
m.volume_oi.mechanism: Volume and open interest proxy for how many participants have priced the contract and therefore how efficient the price is likely to be.
m.volume_oi.rationale: High-volume markets (game winners, totals) are typically priced by more informed flow than thin player props; a model needs a different shrinkage toward the market in each regime. Subtle: volume surges in the final hour often coincide with lineup news and are not directional by themselves.
m.volume_oi.measurement: Cumulative and last-hour volume, open interest, number of distinct trades from the trade tape; bucket markets by liquidity tier and estimate market-vs-model weight per tier.

m.ladder_structure.label: Cross-rung consistency of the threshold ladder (monotonicity, implied distribution)
m.ladder_structure.mechanism: Rungs of a threshold ladder (e.g. 4+, 5+, 6+) must imply one coherent count distribution; deviations expose stale or mispriced rungs and reveal the market's implied mean and variance.
m.ladder_structure.rationale: Ladders for the same player/game are strongly correlated, so edges on adjacent rungs are not independent bets and exposure must be sized per ladder. Subtle: because each rung is a survival probability P(X>=k), monotone non-increasing is a hard constraint, and fitting a Poisson/negative-binomial to the rungs gives an implied mean that can be compared to a model mean on a like-for-like basis.
m.ladder_structure.measurement: For each event/player collect all live rungs at one timestamp; check P(k) non-increasing; fit a discrete distribution (Poisson, negative binomial, or free-form isotonic) to mid prices; compare implied mean/variance and per-rung residual to the model; track which rungs the market lags when news arrives.

m.settlement_truth.label: Settled result, settlement value and timestamp
m.settlement_truth.mechanism: The settled value is the only ground truth for calibrating every other input and exposes rule-edge cases (overtime, voids, delayed games).
m.settlement_truth.rationale: Without exact settlement values, hit rates and calibration are computed against a proxy (box score) that may differ from Kalshi's source (official stats, correction windows). Subtle: stat corrections after the game (scoring changes, hit/error changes, assist reassignments) can flip a threshold, so the settlement timestamp and source matter.
m.settlement_truth.measurement: Join Kalshi settled result and settlement_value to the official box score by game id; flag disagreements and post-game scoring changes; keep settlement time minus game end time.

m.rules_text.label: Versioned rules_primary / settlement wording (OT, ties, postponement, void)
m.rules_text.mechanism: The settlement wording defines which events count (overtime, extra innings, shootout goals, delayed games, DNPs) and therefore changes the true probability of the same real-world sport.
m.rules_text.rationale: Identical-looking contracts can differ: whether overtime/extra innings counts, whether a player who does not play voids or settles at zero, how postponements and shortened games resolve, which official stat source governs. A model that ignores the wording mis-prices the tail. Subtle: wording changes between series/seasons, so it must be versioned per ticker rather than assumed.
m.rules_text.measurement: Pull rules_primary/rules_secondary per market and hash it; extract flags (counts_overtime, counts_shootout, void_if_dnp, postponement_rule, source) by pattern matching and manual review of each new template; join to every training row.

m.external_lines.label: Sportsbook / exchange reference prices with timestamps
m.external_lines.mechanism: Sharp sportsbook and exchange lines are a competing aggregation of information and the standard benchmark for fair probability.
m.external_lines.rationale: Using a de-vigged external line as a feature or benchmark is often a stronger baseline than any public-stats model, and disagreement with Kalshi flags either a stale Kalshi quote or a rule-wording difference. Subtle: books price different settlement terms (e.g. regulation vs including overtime, 'action' rules on postponements) so lines must be mapped to the Kalshi rule before comparison, and the timestamp of the line matters.
m.external_lines.measurement: Capture timestamped lines per book; de-vig (power or Shin method) per market; map to the Kalshi contract's rule (regulation vs full game, push handling); compute Kalshi minus consensus and closing-line value relative to the latest pregame consensus.

m.fees.label: Fee schedule and maker/taker rules in force
m.fees.mechanism: Fees reduce realized edge and depend on price level, so the break-even probability differs by rung and by maker/taker role.
m.fees.rationale: Because the fee is price-dependent, a fixed edge in cents is worth less near 50 than at the tails or vice versa depending on schedule; a model signal must clear fee-adjusted breakeven, not raw midpoint difference. Subtle: fee schedules change over time and by market type, so the version in force at trade time must be used.
m.fees.measurement: Version the fee formula from Kalshi's published fee schedule; compute breakeven probability per price and role; subtract from model edge before any threshold decision.
free_sources: Kalshi fee schedule PDF/help center (kalshi.com/fee-schedule) and /exchange/schedule API

m.lifecycle.label: Open/close/halt/postponement lifecycle events
m.lifecycle.mechanism: Market open, close, halts and postponement events determine when information can be traded on and which pregame snapshot is the last valid one.
m.lifecycle.rationale: Markets may close at scheduled start, on delay, or be extended; late-news windows (confirmed lineup/goalie) may fall before or after the close. Subtle: delayed or postponed games shift the effective decision time and can leave stale quotes, which also mislabels the 'closing' price used for CLV.
m.lifecycle.measurement: Record open_time, close_time, status transitions, and actual first pitch/puck drop from the league feed; define the last-valid-pregame timestamp as min(close_time, actual start); flag delayed/postponed games.

m.strike_hit_rates.label: Historical realized frequency by strike/rung per family (from settlements)
m.strike_hit_rates.mechanism: Realized frequency by rung gives the unconditional base rate that every conditional model must beat, and reveals persistent biases in how thresholds are set.
m.strike_hit_rates.rationale: Markets often over- or under-price specific rung shapes (round-number thresholds, longshot tails). Base rates by rung, season, venue and liquidity tier reveal where the market is calibrated and where it is not. Subtle: settled history is selection-biased by which strikes Kalshi chose to list, so rates are conditional on being listed.

m.trade_tape.label: Executed trades (price, size, taker side, time) for slippage and flow
m.trade_tape.mechanism: Executed trades reveal where size actually transacted, the taker side, and the speed at which price reacts to news.
m.trade_tape.rationale: Trade flow around lineup/goalie/pitcher confirmation shows how quickly information is incorporated; sustained one-sided taker flow can indicate informed trading. Subtle: only executed prints are observable, resting orders are not, so slippage estimates from the tape understate the cost of crossing a thin book.
m.trade_tape.measurement: Pull trades per ticker with timestamps; compute signed volume (taker side), VWAP in windows around news timestamps, post-trade price drift as an informed-flow proxy; estimate slippage by size bucket.

game_side.target: Which team wins the game (and by how many runs for spread/margin contracts), settled after the final out including extra innings unless the wording says otherwise.
game_side.mechanism: Win probability follows from the expected run difference: starter run prevention for the innings he works, bullpen quality for the rest, lineup quality against the specific starter's handedness and arsenal, and park/weather/umpire scaling of both offences. Home field adds a small edge. Because late information (confirmed lineups, scratched starter, weather) moves the line, the model's value comes from timely incorporation and from regressing luck-heavy team results; margin and spread contracts additionally need the run-difference distribution including extra-innings tie breaking.

Expected innings decide how much the bullpen pitches.
Confirmed lineup replaces probable lineups; absent stars change offence.
Lineup quality against this starter's handedness is the offence driver.
Bullpen availability decides run prevention after the starter exits.
Quality of relievers beyond fatigue snapshot.
Park scales run environment for both teams.
Temperature and wind modify scoring and so margins.
Zone size modestly shifts walks, strikeouts and runs.
Fielding and framing adjust runs allowed.
Late scratches or IL moves change the lineup or starter after markets open.
Record vs run differential gap measures luck to regress.
Run-difference distribution needed for spread and margin rungs.
Ghost-runner extras settle ties in including-extras contracts.
Price moves after lineup confirmation show how news was priced.
Sharp-line benchmark for fair probability.
Spread and depth decide whether a modelled edge survives execution costs.
Price-dependent fees set the breakeven probability for the edge.
Trade flow around lineup confirmation shows speed and direction of information incorporation.
Settlement values calibrate the model and expose extra-innings, shortened-game and correction edge cases.

interactions.hypothesis: Starter quality only matters for the innings he pitches, so starter edge should be weighted by expected batters faced and the quality gap to the bullpen that replaces him.
Lineup handedness against starter handedness: a platoon-weak confirmed lineup lowers team strength more than season-level wRC+ suggests, so team offence should be lineup-by-hand specific.
Wind and park interact: wind-out adds more runs in HR-friendly parks and for fly-ball pitchers, so the effect should be multiplied with park HR factor and pitcher fly-ball rate.

game_total.target: Total runs (or one team's runs) in the game, with the contract defining whether extra-innings runs count and how shortened games settle.
game_total.mechanism: Expected runs are the sum over plate appearances of per-PA run value, determined by starter quality for the early innings, bullpen quality for the late innings, the lineups' quality by handedness, park and weather (air density, wind), and the umpire's zone. Run distributions are overdispersed and clustered by inning, so threshold prices depend on dispersion and not just the mean; late-breaking information (confirmed lineups, wind, roof status, scratched starters) is the main source of mispricing.

Contact quality and defence determine hits allowed.
Overdispersion and tail shape for rungs.
League baseline run environment for the season.
Extra innings add runs if counted.

interactions.hypothesis: Wind, temperature and park multiply: the same wind adds more in a HR-friendly park and in hot, thin air, so the weather effect must be estimated with park interaction terms.

Starter quality x expected innings x bullpen quality: run total is a mixture of starter-run-rate and bullpen-run-rate by innings, so the starter's hook probability interacts with the bullpen's quality.
Umpire zone x pitcher type: a large zone lowers totals more for hitters' counts and for command pitchers than for high-walk pitchers, so the umpire effect depends on pitcher walk profile.

player_hit.target: Hitter counting outcomes in a game: hits, total bases, RBIs, runs or stolen bases (threshold ladders), requiring the player to appear per the wording.
player_hit.mechanism: Each count is the sum over the hitter's plate appearances of per-PA outcome probabilities, so expected value = expected PA (lineup slot, team scoring, substitution risk) x per-PA rates (contact quality, K/BB, platoon, pitch-type matchup, park, weather, defence) with the opposing starter's quality for the first two or three PAs and the bullpen for the rest. RBI, runs and SB additionally depend on teammates' on-base and the situation, making them more variable and less skill-pure.

inputs.why: PA volume by lineup slot and team total is the multiplier.
Per-PA outcome rates are the base.
Contact quality predicts hits and total bases beyond results.
Handedness matchup with the starter and relievers.
Matchup of hitter's pitch-type weaknesses vs the starter's arsenal.
Starter quality adjusts per-PA outcomes in early PAs.
Bullpen quality for later PAs.
Confirmed batting slot and participation.
Park hit/TB factors by handedness.
Weather influences ball carry and extra-base hits.
Defence converts contact to outs.
BABIP luck regression for hits.
Count distribution given PA and rates.
Runners on base ahead for RBIs.
Steal context for SB legs: steal attempts depend on the runner, the pitcher's delivery time to the plate and the catcher's throw.
Hits/TB rungs for one player are nested.
Head-to-head history is quoted often but is tiny-sample; included to test the null against pitch-type matchup.

interactions.hypothesis: PA count x per-PA probability: a bottom-order hitter with equal skill gets fewer PAs; expected hits thus depend jointly on slot and team total.
Pitch-type matchup x platoon: a hitter's weakness to breaking balls matters more against same-handed breaking-ball-heavy starters, so platoon and pitch-mix effects should be modelled jointly.
BABIP luck x contact quality: recent hit totals overstate skill when xBA lags, so xBA-based projections should replace observed hits.

period.target: First-five-innings (F5) results and totals (and similar inning-window markets): winner, margin and total runs through a set inning.
period.mechanism: F5 isolates starters: run scoring is determined by the starters' quality over their first two trips through the order, the lineups' strength against them, park and weather, with the bullpen entering only when the starter is pulled early. Starter exit probability before the fifth is the major structural uncertainty and ties are possible, so rules matter (push vs loss).

Separates the starter-only portion from the bullpen.
Third-time-through penalty affects innings 5-6.
Probability of early exit before the fifth.
Lineup vs starter handedness: a team's lineup quality against the starter's handedness determines runs in the early innings, more than overall season team offence.
Confirmed batting order: who bats and in what order determines the actual hitters a pitcher faces and the plate appearances each hitter gets.
Run environment for early innings.
Weather scaling: temperature, air density and wind change ball flight, so fly-ball outcomes (HR, doubles) vary with conditions.
Zone effects on early innings.
Contact allowed and defence: hits allowed depend on the quality of contact against a pitcher and the fielders converting it into outs.
Overdispersed distribution for the first five.
Tie/push treatment and shortened-game handling.

interactions.hypothesis: Starter exit before the fifth is a mixture: P(early exit) x bullpen quality vs P(full five) x starter quality, so leash and bullpen state interact with starter quality in F5.
Top-of-order exposure: in F5 each starter faces the top of the order twice or more, so top-of-order quality vs handedness is heavier-weighted than in full game.
F5 tie probability is high enough that spread/winner contracts differ by tie rule; the rules interact with run-distribution shape.

player_pitch.target: Starting pitcher counting stats: strikeouts or outs recorded in the game (threshold ladder), requiring the pitcher to start per the wording.
player_pitch.mechanism: Strikeouts = batters faced x per-PA K probability and outs = batters faced x (1 - on-base events), so the outcome is workload times rate. Workload (batters faced) is limited by the pitch cap divided by pitches per PA and by performance-based hooks (the manager's leash, times-through-order, score), while the per-PA K probability combines the pitcher's pitch-level whiff ability with the confirmed lineup's whiff and K tendencies by handedness, modulated by the umpire's zone, catcher framing and park, and diminishing across the order. Realized pitch count is not known pregame; only its distribution is.

Pitch-level whiff drives strikeouts.

Lineup patience reduces BF per pitch.

Zone size alters called strikes.

Velocity changes indicate fatigue or injury.
Bullpen availability influences the hook.
Park/altitude affects pitch movement and strikeout rates.
Cold or hot affects velocity and grip.
Opener usage makes the listed pitcher's BF tiny or void.
Strikeout rungs share a latent mean and dispersion.
A plate-appearance simulation turns pitch cap, hook and per-PA K into a full strikeout distribution.

interactions.hypothesis: Pitch mix x lineup whiff by pitch: the strikeout rate is the usage-weighted sum of pitcher whiff and lineup whiff for each pitch type, not the product of aggregate K% rates.

Times-through-order x hook: the K rate decays by trip while the probability of reaching the third trip depends on pitch count and leash, so expected K is a sum over trips weighted by survival probabilities.

Umpire zone x called-strike rate: a larger zone helps pitchers who live on the edges (high called-strike rate), a smaller zone helps hitters, so the umpire effect should be scaled by the pitcher's edge-pitch share and catcher framing.
Pitch cap x efficiency x patience: outs scale with pitch cap divided by pitches per PA, which depends on the opposing lineup's patience, so the cap and lineup patience interact for outs markets.

mentions.target: Whether a specific word or phrase is spoken during a specified broadcast, per the contract's source and counting rules.
mentions.mechanism: Mentions depend on the announcers' vocabulary and on game events that trigger topics (milestones, pitching changes, weather), so the best-supported hypotheses concern crew habits, broadcast length and event likelihood; sports performance statistics have little direct predictive role. This is close to a novelty/language market with limited statistical structure and sparse history.

interactions.hypothesis: Crew vocabulary x event triggers: the probability of a word equals baseline crew rate plus a trigger bump when the relevant event occurs, so event likelihood should be modelled separately.
Airtime length: delays and extra innings lengthen the broadcast, raising the chance of any word, so game-length uncertainty interacts with word rate.

Late-season results matter less if ballots are cast before the postseason.

off_field.target: Non-game events (business, league announcements, non-baseball questions) settled by public announcement or defined sources.
off_field.mechanism: These markets depend on organisational decisions and external events rather than on-field performance. There is no strong statistical structure; value, if any, comes from reference-class frequencies, calendar constraints and timestamped news relative to the resolution wording. Many are effectively novelty markets with weak predictability from baseball data.

hitter_hits_and_total_bases.target: Whether a hitter records at least k hits, total bases or H+R+RBI in the game, requiring appearance per the wording.
hitter_hits_and_total_bases.mechanism: Hits and total bases are sums over plate appearances of per-PA outcome probabilities (single, double, triple, HR vs out), so the expected value is expected PAs (lineup slot, team scoring, substitution risk) times per-PA rates and the distribution is a compound binomial/multinomial. Per-PA rates combine the hitter's contact quality, K and BB, platoon, pitch-type matchup against the starter, park and weather, defence, and later the bullpen; BABIP luck regresses. H+R+RBI adds team-dependent components (runners ahead, hitters behind), increasing variance and correlation with team scoring.

Confirmed slot and participation define PAs.
True-talent per-PA outcome rates with projections.
xBA/xSLG and barrel% predict hits/TB beyond results.
Handedness split against starter and bullpen.
Hitter's pitch-type performance against the starter's arsenal.

Starter's contact suppression and defence behind him.
Relief quality for late PAs: relief pitchers' quality sets run prevention after the starter exits, determining full-game total and winner.
Park hit and TB factors by handedness.
Weather influences extra-base hit rates.

Small, shrunk correction for role/injury changes.

Runs component needs on-base skill and hitters behind.

interactions.hypothesis: PA count x per-PA probability: expected hits = expected PA x P(hit per PA); the lineup slot and team total shift PA while contact quality shifts probability, so both must be in one compound model.
Platoon x pitch-type matchup: same-handed breaking-ball-heavy starters suppress hitters with weak breaking-ball performance, so platoon and pitch-mix effects interact rather than add.
Contact quality x defence/park: expected TB depends on how hard and where a hitter hits the ball relative to park dimensions and fielders, so xSLG should be park- and defence-adjusted.
BABIP luck x recent form: recent hot hitting driven by BABIP should not move the projection, so recent form should enter through contact quality, not batting average.

hitter_home_runs.label: Hitter home runs (1+ / 2+)
hitter_home_runs.target: Whether a hitter hits at least one (or two) home runs in the game, requiring appearance per the wording.
hitter_home_runs.mechanism: HR per game = 1 - product over PAs of (1 - p_HR), where per-PA HR probability multiplies the hitter's fly-ball/pull/barrel profile by the pitcher's HR vulnerability (by handedness and pitch type), the park's handedness-specific HR factor and the weather (wind component, temperature/air density). Because the base probability is low, multiplicative environment shifts matter and the dominant uncertainty is Bernoulli luck; HR/FB regresses to a contact-quality-determined mean. PA count (batting slot) and the bullpen's HR vulnerability also matter.

inputs.why: Barrel%, pull-air%, FB% and max EV predict HR beyond past HR totals.
Bat speed/squared-up rate adds a stabilising early power signal.
Barrel and hard-hit rates supplement the HR profile.
Pitcher's HR/FB, barrels and fly-ball rate allowed by hand.
Park HR factor by handedness and ball carry environment.
Wind out/in component along the hitter's pull side.
Temperature/humidity/altitude change carry.
Handedness matchup influences HR rate.
Fastball-hitter vs fastball-heavy pitcher matchup.
PA multiplier by slot and team total.
Confirmed lineup and slot: who bats and in what order determines the actual hitters a pitcher faces and the plate appearances each hitter gets.
Later PAs face relievers with different HR vulnerability.
Regress hot/cold HR/FB luck: home runs per fly ball regress strongly to a mean determined by park and contact quality, so past HR luck is not persistent.
1+ and 2+ HR rungs are nested and linked to total HR environment.
Appearance requirement and settlement for postponed/shortened games.

interactions.hypothesis: Hitter pull-air profile x park pull-side HR factor x wind: HR probability depends on the hitter's spray direction relative to the park's short side and the wind along that line, so the three should be modelled jointly.
Barrel rate x pitcher HR vulnerability x pitch type: HR risk is highest when a hitter's strong pitch type meets a pitcher who throws it in the damage zone, so matchup is by pitch type and zone.
Air density x wind x park: warm, thin air plus out-blowing wind in a short-porch park compound, but are already partially included in park factors, so use deviation from park norms.
PA count x per-PA HR rate: because per-PA HR probability is small, extra PA from batting slot or team scoring matters almost linearly, interacting with lineup posting and substitution risk.

hitter_rbis_runs_sb.label: Hitter RBIs, runs scored and stolen bases
hitter_rbis_runs_sb.target: Whether a hitter records at least k RBIs or stolen bases in the game (runs and combos via H+R+RBI are in the hits archetype), requiring appearance per the wording.
hitter_rbis_runs_sb.mechanism: RBI depend on the number of runners on base when the hitter bats (OBP of hitters ahead, team scoring) and the hitter's ability to drive them in (power, contact, situational), so they are heavily context-dependent and high-variance, with lineup slot and team total dominating. Stolen bases require reaching base, deciding to attempt (runner speed, manager, game state) and succeeding against the pitcher's hold time and the catcher's arm, a low-frequency event with rule-regime shifts (pickoff limits, bigger bases). Both markets depend on lineup confirmation and on the opposing starter and catcher.

PA multiplier and slot effects.
Confirmed slot and surrounding hitters.

Steal attempt context: pitcher hold time, catcher pop time.
Runner attempt and success rates.

Manager aggressiveness and platoon/pinch-hit style.

Count distribution for RBI thresholds.
Appearance requirement and SB/CS scoring definitions.
Rungs for the same player share latent opportunity.

interactions.hypothesis: RBI opportunity x power: RBI = (runners on base when batting) x (conversion given hitter), so on-base skill of preceding batters should multiply the hitter's extra-base and contact skill rather than add.

SB attempt: runner speed x pitcher hold time x catcher arm x game state; each factor changes both attempt and success and they must be combined (a slow pitcher with a weak catcher invites attempts by fast runners).
Reaching base x attempt: P(SB) requires the runner to reach first or second, so OBP and expected PA interact with attempt rate, making lineup slot critical.
Rule regime x manager style: the post-2023 rules raised attempts, but managers differ in green-light rates, so regime baselines should be interacted with team style.

game_moneyline.label: Game winner, run line and winning margin
game_moneyline.target: Which team wins the game (including extra innings unless worded otherwise), covers a run spread, or wins by a particular margin.
game_moneyline.mechanism: Win probability is built from expected run scoring and prevention for each team at the plate-appearance level: starter quality and expected innings, bullpen quality and availability, confirmed lineup quality against the starter's hand and arsenal, defence, park and weather and the umpire's zone, with a modest home-field effect. The win probability is a function of the run-difference distribution (overdispersed, with extra-innings resolution of ties), so run line and margin contracts need the full distribution rather than the moneyline alone. Late information (confirmed lineups, scratched starters, weather/roof) is the main edge source, and records must be regressed to run-based talent.

Expected innings determine starter vs bullpen weight.
Confirmed lineup strength vs starter handedness.
Lineup confirmation and rest-day sit-downs.

Weather and wind: temperature, air density and wind change ball flight, so fly-ball outcomes (HR, doubles) vary with conditions.

Run-difference distribution for spread and margin.
Extra-innings resolution of ties.
Opponent-adjusted team strength.

interactions.hypothesis: Starter innings x bullpen gap: the effective edge from a better starter equals quality gap times expected innings, plus bullpen gap times remaining innings, so workload and bullpen quality should be combined into a weighted pitching rating.

Confirmed lineup x starter handedness x arsenal: lineup strength should be platoon- and pitch-type-specific, so a rested star or lefty-heavy lineup against a righty changes team strength beyond season wRC+.

Run-line cover depends on distribution: favourites win by 2+ less often than win probability suggests because of one-run games and bullpen use when ahead, so margin should come from the run distribution and late-game leverage.
Lineup/starter confirmation timing x price: markets open before lineups, so the edge is how fast the model reprices on confirmation relative to the quote history.

game_total_and_team_total.label: Game total and team total runs
game_total_and_team_total.target: Whether total runs (or one team's runs) exceed a threshold under the contract's scope (including extra innings, shortened game rules).
game_total_and_team_total.mechanism: Expected runs = sum over plate appearances of per-PA run value for each team, driven by starter quality over the innings he pitches, bullpen run rate for the rest, the lineups' quality by handedness, and multiplicative park/weather/air-density and umpire effects; the realised distribution is overdispersed and inning-clustered so thresholds price tail probabilities. Team totals isolate one offence against the opposing pitching staff and defence. The main edges are late environmental/lineup information (wind, roof, confirmed lineup, scratched starter) and correct dispersion and regression of luck.

interactions.hypothesis: Wind x air density x park: HR/fly-ball effects are multiplicative in HR-friendly parks, so weather adjustments should be computed from deviations from park norms and interacted with park HR factor and fly-ball tendencies.
Starter exit x bullpen state: totals are a mixture of starter and bullpen run rates by inning, so starter workload and bullpen availability/quality interact to give the late-inning scoring.
Umpire zone x walk-prone pitcher/lineup: a small zone raises totals most when a pitcher is walk-prone and lineups are patient, so umpire effects should depend on plate-discipline matchup.
Dispersion x threshold: high-total and low-total rungs price tails; park and weather affect variance as well as mean (Coors, wind games), so dispersion should depend on environment.

first_inning_and_inning_markets.label: First-inning runs and inning-level markets
first_inning_and_inning_markets.target: Whether runs are scored in a specific inning (first inning or other inning), which team outscores the other in the inning, or the inning's run total.
first_inning_and_inning_markets.mechanism: An inning is a short Markov process through base-out states with outcomes depending on the three hitters due up and the pitcher on the mound; for the first inning the top three of each lineup face the fresh starter, so the run probability (YRFI) is the union of two half-innings with probabilities driven by top-order on-base skill, handedness and starter first-trip command. Later-inning markets additionally depend on which batters are due, TTO penalty and bullpen entry, which are partly unknowable pregame. Small samples make historical first-inning splits mostly noise; PA-level simulation is preferred.

Top-of-order quality and starter first-inning profile.
Confirmed top-three hitters and order.
Handedness of top-order hitters vs starter.
Starter quality in the first trip through the order.
Early walks and zone rate: walks arise when pitchers miss the zone and hitters take pitches outside it; both the pitcher's command and the lineup's discipline matter.
K% reduces baserunners: strikeouts occur when a pitcher's swing-and-miss and called-strike ability meet hitters prone to striking out; lineup K% by handedness captures the hitter side.
First-three-innings pattern: the first three innings give every starter a full turn through the top of the order and are mostly pitcher-quality and lineup-top dependent.
Later-inning markets depend on trip through order.
Bullpen entry for later innings.

Inning-level distribution: runs per team per game are overdispersed and inning-clustered, so threshold and total markets depend on distribution shape and the correlation between teams.

interactions.hypothesis: Top-three OBP x starter command: first-inning scoring requires baserunners from top hitters against the starter's zone and walk rate, so the product by half-inning and the two-half-inning union give the event probability.

Handedness x starter first-trip arsenal: lefty-heavy top order against a righty with a weak changeup changes first-inning run probability beyond aggregate wRC+, so platoon should be applied to the top three.
Small-sample first-inning splits x PA-level simulation: observed first-inning ERA is mostly noise, so it should enter only as a heavily shrunk adjustment to the PA-level model.

first5_markets.label: First-five-innings winner, spread and total
first5_markets.target: First-five-innings result (winner/run spread) or total runs through five innings.
first5_markets.mechanism: Through five innings runs are scored mostly against the starters (typically two trips through the order), so the market is driven by starter quality, expected exit before the fifth, the lineups' strength against the starter's hand, and the environment, with the bullpen entering only after early exits. Relative to full game, bullpen strength is de-emphasised and starter leash risk is emphasised, and ties are possible so spread and winner contracts differ by tie handling.

interactions.hypothesis: Exit before the fifth: F5 run rate is a mixture of starter-only and bullpen-inclusive, so leash and bullpen state interact with starter quality.
Top-of-order exposure x handedness: in five innings the top of the lineup bats twice, so platoon quality of the top six hitters is weighted more than in a full game.
Tie handling x run distribution: F5 ties are common enough that push/loss rules change pricing; the discrete distribution and rule jointly define the probability.

extras_and_delay.label: Extra innings and game delay/postponement
extras_and_delay.target: Whether the game goes to extra innings (tied after nine) or whether a delay/postponement occurs, per the contract definition.
extras_and_delay.mechanism: Extra innings are the event that the two run totals tie after nine, so probability is a function of the run distribution (higher in low-total, close games) and of late-inning scoring, with the ghost runner shaping what happens after but not the event. Delay markets are weather-timing problems: probability of precipitation or lightning near first pitch relative to roof status and umpire/team decision behaviour, mostly independent of team quality. Both are low-to-moderate probability events decided by distributional shape and exact contract wording (start delay vs in-game delay, suspended-game treatment).

Strong starters lower scoring and increase tie chance.

Low-scoring environments tie more.
Extra-inning strategy affects length of extras.

Lightning, wind and temperature.
Delay, suspension and postponement definitions.
Contract wording for extras and delay windows.
Market close vs actual first pitch time.

interactions.hypothesis: Total x spread: tie probability peaks when expected total is low and teams are evenly matched, so total and spread jointly drive extra-innings probability and should come from one run-distribution model.
Precipitation timing x roof state: the same forecast produces a delay only if the roof is open and the rain overlaps the game window, so roof state gates the weather risk.

Delay definition x time window: contracts counting only start delays are driven by pre-first-pitch weather, in-game delay contracts add game-length exposure (including extras), so the definition interacts with extra-innings probability.

season_futures.label: Division winner, season wins, postseason futures and series
season_futures.target: Team season outcomes: division title, win total thresholds, playoff/pennant/title futures, postseason series winners, records and specials.
season_futures.mechanism: Futures integrate talent estimates (projection priors updated with run differential, not record) through the remaining schedule with uncertainty, then apply tiebreakers and bracket rules; postseason series switch to a game-level dynamic program using announced starters, rest, bullpen usage and home-field pattern. Long-horizon prices depend on rating uncertainty and slow information (injuries, trades); short-horizon series prices depend on pitching availability and shortened managerial hooks. Luck regression and tiebreaker formalities matter most in close races.

inputs.why: Monte Carlo of the remaining schedule and bracket.
Talent prior from projection systems.
Regress record luck to run differential.
Remaining schedule quality: future opponent quality, home/away split and days off shape expected wins for the remainder of the season.
Injuries to key players and depth.
Rotation quality, especially in October.
Bullpen quality for close games.
Seeding and tiebreaker rules: seeding, wild-card format and tiebreaker rules decide who plays whom and with what home field, determining futures settle paths.
Series state, rest and rotation for series markets.
Postseason pitching usage patterns.
League baselines for season specials.
Trades and call-ups: transactions and news change who plays and the team's strength with a lag before statistics catch up.
Futures benchmark: sharp sportsbook and exchange lines are a competing aggregation of information and the standard benchmark for fair probability.

interactions.hypothesis: Talent uncertainty x series length: greater uncertainty about true strength widens futures outcomes and short series compress the talent gap, so rating uncertainty and format interact.
Luck regression x tiebreakers: simulation should use expected wins for strength but formal tiebreakers for the ties, so regress luck first, apply rules second.
Injury state x remaining schedule: a long-term injury reduces strength for the remainder, with a larger effect when remaining opponents are strong or the margin for playoffs is thin.

season_leaders_and_awards.label: Season leaders, player stat totals and awards
season_leaders_and_awards.target: Leader of a statistical category, a player's season total threshold, or winner of an award (MVP, Cy Young, ROY).
season_leaders_and_awards.mechanism: Season-stat and leader outcomes are current total plus rest-of-season rate times opportunity times availability, so a competitor-level simulation (with correlated team context, injury risk, and qualification rules for rate stats) gives probabilities. Awards add a voter model: production rank, team success and narrative under a specific ballot structure and timing, with finalists as information events. Early-season leaders mostly reflect luck, so regressing rates is the main lever, while late-season markets are dominated by games remaining and injuries.

Qualification x rate stats: borderline players qualify only by PA accrual, so playing time and qualification rules interact in batting-average or ERA leader markets.
Production rank x team success x ballot timing: voters weigh WAR with team outcome and cast ballots at a specific time, so late-season changes matter only before the deadline.

player_participation.label: Player participation (plays / starts / appears)
player_participation.target: Whether a named player plays or starts in a game, per the contract's definition.
player_participation.mechanism: Participation is determined by manager decisions (rest days, platoon sits), injury status and late scratches, resolved mostly when the lineup card posts; before then it is a probability from rest-day patterns, handedness of the opposing starter and injury news, afterwards it is near-certain except for in-game substitution cases. The edge is timing relative to market close and the exact definition (starts vs appears).

Starter/platoon/bench role: a player's role determines whether he starts and how many PAs he gets, which drives participation and counting-stat markets.
Rest after night games and travel.

Manager platoon and substitution style.

Lineup posting time x market close: probabilities are mixtures until the card posts, so the posting timestamp relative to close defines the information advantage.
Injury vintage x scratch risk: players listed day-to-day have elevated scratch probability late, so injury reports and warm-up news interact with lineup confirmation.

announcer_mentions.label: Broadcast word-mention markets
announcer_mentions.target: Whether a specified word or phrase is spoken in the named broadcast, per the contract's source and counting rules.
announcer_mentions.mechanism: Mention probability reflects announcer vocabulary (crew-specific base rates), the length of the broadcast and events that trigger topics (milestones, pitching changes, weather delays, named players), with the contract's definition of which feed and what counts. Baseball statistics offer little direct signal, so this is closer to a novelty/language market with sparse history; the best hypotheses concern crew habits and trigger events.

Storylines and events that trigger words.
Recent storylines that announcers will discuss.

Broadcast length x word rate: delays and extra innings lengthen the broadcast, so game-length uncertainty interacts with word rate.
Wording x feed: national vs local feeds differ and the contract defines the counted feed, so crew identity interacts with rules text.

transactions.label: Transactions, coaching and personnel events
transactions.target: Whether a trade, signing, call-up, extension or manager/coach change occurs by a given date.
transactions.mechanism: Transactions follow institutional calendars and team incentives: standing (buyer vs seller), contract status, roster-rule constraints and front-office behaviour, with beat-writer reports preceding many official moves. The probability is a hazard over the contract window, estimated from reference classes and updated by reports and standings, with the resolution defined by official announcement.

Report credibility x price reaction: price changes after reports measure their credibility and the rules define whether they count.

offfield_markets.label: Business, non-baseball and esports novelty markets
offfield_markets.target: Events outside baseball games settled by public announcement or defined sources.
offfield_markets.mechanism: These markets are driven by organisational decisions and external events rather than on-field performance. There is little statistical structure: the best-supported hypotheses are reference-class frequencies, calendar constraints and timestamped news relative to the resolution wording. Non-baseball and esports items are not predicted by baseball inputs at all and should be treated as novelty markets with no baseball model.

News timing x resolution source: reports precede official announcements, so price reaction must be read against what the rules count.
